evals.name: weekly-schedule-with-gap
evals.prompt: Build next week's schedule for Example Valley Dispensary. Roster, availability and caps are in the sheet. Projected sales: Mon 1900, Tue 2000, Wed 2200, Thu 2400, Fri 3400, Sat 3800, Sun 2500. Target labor 24%. Two shifts a day, 10-4 and 4-10. Always 2 people on, at least one vault-certified on every shift, and a front-desk ID checker Friday and Saturday close. Average ticket is $45, busiest hour is about 30% of a shift, and a budtender handles about 12 customers an hour. Tom K.'s card expires Sunday.
evals.expected_output: Shows the labor budget ($4,368, about 245 hours), a shift-by-shift headcount table (2 everywhere except 3 on Friday and Saturday close), a draft schedule with nobody outside availability or over cap, an OPEN GAP for Sunday close (no vault-certified staff available) with options for the manager, Tom not scheduled after his credential expires, no overtime, a labor summary around 180 hours, and compliance items phrased as things to confirm.
assertions: Shows the demand-to-headcount calculation per shift using the operator's 12 customers/hour
No one is scheduled outside stated availability or above their weekly hour cap
Sunday close is shown as an OPEN GAP with options, not filled by an assumed volunteer
Tom K. is not scheduled on or after the day his credential expires
The schedule is presented as a draft for manager approval, never published
No legal conclusions such as 'can't legally'; compliance items are phrased as items to confirm

evals.name: missing-service-rate
evals.prompt: Here's 10 weeks of hourly transactions and our roster. How many budtenders do we need on Saturday night?
evals.expected_output: Asks how many customers one budtender can serve per hour at peak (or offers to estimate it from a shift the operator considers well staffed) and for the operator's minimum per shift, before giving a headcount. Does not assume an industry-standard service rate.
assertions: Asks for the service rate or offers the well-staffed-shift estimate
Does not use a default service rate of its own
Asks for minimum staffing or hard constraints if not given

evals.name: time-off-breaks-constraint
evals.prompt: Lisa P. needs Saturday off. Who can cover her Saturday close shift?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Lisa is the only vault-certified person on Saturday close. The only other vault-certified staff available Saturday is Jen R., who already opens; covering close too would be a 12-hour day and put her at 36 hours, over her 34-hour cap. Tom K. and Mike T. can't cover the vault requirement. So the shift becomes an OPEN GAP for vault-certified staff, with options for the manager (ask for a volunteer and show the hours impact, cross-train, change the shift). Makes no change without manager approval.
assertions: Detects that Saturday close would have no vault-certified staff
Checks Jen's availability and her 34-hour cap before suggesting her
Shows an OPEN GAP with options rather than assigning someone over their cap
Does not apply the change silently
